div.head: Hn Lond 3
div.ab: Et si quis ciuium de placitis corone implacitatus fuerit, per sacramentum, quod iudicatum fuerit in ciuitate, se disrationet homo Londoñ.
Et si quis civium de placitis coronae implacitatus fuerit, per sacramentum quod iudicatum fuerit in civitate, se disrationet homo London.
And if any of the citizens has become involved in a plea of the crown, he shall clear himself, as a citizen of London, by an oath which has been decreed in the city.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 288–289 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 525, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: secundum antiquam consuetudinem civitatis setzt dafür Freibrief 1155. Gemeint ist die Reinigung mit 36, 12, 6 Eideshelfern (s. d. Gl 45b), auf welche die Urteilfindung in London erkennt.—Den Satz benutzt Colchester 1189.—Stubbs missversteht das [nur des Nachdruckes wegen ans Ende gestellte] Subjekt: ‘als einen Bürger’; solcher Stil aber wäre zu klassisch. Zu beweisen ist nicht das Bürgerrecht, sondern die Leugnung der Kronklage. S. Gl Kronprozess 15—19

The charter of 1155 puts secundum antiquam consuetudinem civitatis in its place. What is meant is purgation with 36, 12 or 6 oath-helpers (see that word in Gl 45b), which the judgment-finding in London awards.—Colchester 1189 makes use of the sentence.—Stubbs misunderstands the subject [placed at the end only for emphasis]: ‘as a citizen’; such a style, however, would be too classical. What has to be proved is not citizenship but the denial of the crown plea. See Gl Kronprozess 15—19
